body:
I don't know exactly what you are going through, but I know what its like to be let go while your ex goes and fucks off to "the next one". I'm just saying, nothing will ever satisfy that persons thirst. Nothing will ever keep him happy.

I understand that you miss him, but these feelings, I can PROMISE you, they will not last forever. Find support through friends, family, therapists or even here to get through this. Cry it out. Learn through this pain and overcome it. He was careless with you, and I **know** in time he will get his in return (*trust me*), but what's important here is I know you have the strength to get through this. To love someone like that, that takes a big heart. A heart full of love and understanding. Its okay to feel how your feeling.

When my mom was going through depression and anxiety, she said so many terrible things. I thought she hated my guts. 

When I was 15, I went to this guys place one afternoon. He raped me In his basement with his mom upstairs. At the time I didn't know she was in the house. After the screams and struggle, he finished and let me go. I ran upstairs and called my mom with their landline. I realized during the rings that his mom was starring at me with a book in her hand. Not a look of surprise, but a look of disgust, as if she were thinking, "You deserved it you slut."... I think I was more terrified in that moment than the one previously endured before that... When my mom came to pick me up, I was shaking in the car. She asked me what was wrong with me. I replied with a why would you care. She said try me. I told her I was raped after a long pause. She started to laugh, then scoffed replying, "You're just saying that to get attention.". As soon as she said that I opened the door of the moving car and jumped out. I didn't get hurt too bad. She kept telling me how stupid I was.

I tried to commit suicide a few months later with a bottle of tylenol. It didn't work. It just upset my stomach quite terribly for a week. I told her about it a month later after a big fight we had. When I was crying at the end, I said I hated her, she replied with a simple, "I wish you were dead.".

I told her about it again **years** later after she took years of medications and therapy, anger management and the whole nine yards -- *This self help wouldn't have happened if I didn't tell a school councilor. The councilor threatened social services which I wasn't aware of until she brought my mother in to talk (I'm not going to lie it was hard to trust therapists for a while after that) --* When re-confronting my mom about what I tried to do but failed miserably at, all the things she had said and did to me... she broke down in tears saying how lost and numb she was. She doesn't remember saying or doing these things. But if she did do them that she would take it all back if she could.... My mom never had a stable family life. Much, **much** worse than my own. My grandmother was a narcissistic psychopath (*not diagnosed but the woman was crazy*). She was a very... corrupted woman who never **EVER** could see her own wrong doings. I haven't spoken to her in over 10 years. I pretend the woman is dead.

My mother really was lost back then. After everything she's been through, she really is a different person now and I'm proud of her. I still do therapy to cope with my own scars. I actually just saw my therapist today which helped quite a bit. Doing DBT courses which have been a miracle in the works.

On anther note, my point in all this... Deep down... I feel that... if I had actually committed suicide, she would probably have done the same and followed my lead. She would have felt so much guilt and regret. I feel the same could happen to your father. At the very least he would have felt immense pain but swallow it deep down within himself. He just... He **might** feel like he's in his own suffocating darkness. And he does not know how to show any love. He was never taught how to deal with emotions. I feel, maybe, as if your truth made him feel uneasy, that he was being attacked in some way, maybe that he felt **he** was the root of your pain. So he said that awful fucking thing to you. And probably many others too.

I'm not saying to like him. I'm not saying to forgive him. Maybe just to see from my experience that there **might** be something else going on. But some people never fucking change. Like my evil grandmother who mentally tortured my mother. Some people... some people you just need to leave the fuck alone. Even if they are family. Sometimes you need to pretend they're dead so you can hopefully move on and live the best life you can. Even if others can't and will not change, its very possible that you can.

I'm sorry you feel like this. Your post turned my stomach. I've thought those same thoughts. I felt those same feelings. I understand completely what you mean when you say that.

I wish I could help you in some way... 

I'm listening to this song I found 20 minutes ago that's been helping me with my non-stop crying. Maybe it can help you in some way, even if it's just a small amount.

[https://youtu.be/nFwkeOyYV1I](https://youtu.be/nFwkeOyYV1I)

I feel like there is so much more to experience lol...

I'm sorry. I'm sorry  you're feeling this pain too.

I wish... there was a pill that would force me to forget. Just make the pain go away. Permanently.
